pt.title: "Eleições Serão Realizadas": O que o primeiro discurso de Delcy Rodríguez na ONU revela sobre o caminho pós-Maduro da Venezuela

segments.src: Venezuela's acting president, Delcy Rodríguez, took the podium at the United Nations General Assembly on September 23, 2026, and told world leaders that "elections will be held in Venezuela."
segments.tr: A presidente interina da Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, subiu ao pódio na Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas em 23 de setembro de 2026 e disse aos líderes mundiais que "eleições serão realizadas na Venezuela."

segments.src: What she did not say was when.
segments.tr: O que ela não disse foi quando.

segments.src: Nearly nine months after U.S.
segments.tr: Quase nove meses após as forças dos EUA

segments.src: forces captured Nicolás Maduro in January, the speech offered a promise, a tone of reconciliation with Washington, and very few specifics.
segments.tr: capturarem Nicolás Maduro em janeiro, o discurso ofereceu uma promessa, um tom de reconciliação com Washington e pouquíssimos detalhes.

segments.src: This explainer covers what she said, what was missing, and how the United States and Venezuela's opposition may respond, based on reporting from NBC News, NPR, UPI and analysis from the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS).
segments.tr: Este explicativo aborda o que ela disse, o que faltou e como os Estados Unidos e a oposição da Venezuela podem responder, com base em reportagens da NBC News, NPR, UPI e análises do Centro de Estudos Estratégicos e Internacionais (CSIS).

segments.src: ## Why this speech matters
segments.tr: ## Por que este discurso importa

segments.src: Rodríguez's appearance carried symbolic weight before she said a word.
segments.tr: A aparição de Rodríguez carregava peso simbólico antes mesmo de ela dizer uma palavra.

segments.src: Reports describe it as the first visit to the United States by a Venezuelan head of state since 2018, when Maduro himself traveled to New York for the General Assembly.
segments.tr: Relatos descrevem como a primeira visita aos Estados Unidos de um chefe de estado venezuelano desde 2018, quando o próprio Maduro viajou para Nova York para a Assembleia Geral.

segments.src: She took over after a surprise U.S.
segments.tr: Ela assumiu o poder após uma surpreendente operação militar dos EUA

segments.src: military operation in January that captured Maduro and brought him to the United States to face drug trafficking charges.
segments.tr: em janeiro que capturou Maduro e o levou para os Estados Unidos para enfrentar acusações de tráfico de drogas.

segments.src: Since then, her government and Washington have moved from confrontation toward a working, if uneasy, relationship.
segments.tr: Desde então, seu governo e Washington passaram do confronto para uma relação de trabalho, ainda que tensa.

segments.src: Standing at the UN lectern, Rodríguez was presenting Venezuela's new chapter to the world for the first time.
segments.tr: Em pé na tribuna da ONU, Rodríguez estava apresentando o novo capítulo da Venezuela ao mundo pela primeira vez.

segments.src: ## What she said
segments.tr: ## O que ela disse

segments.src: According to news reports, the main points of the address were:
segments.tr: De acordo com reportagens, os principais pontos do discurso foram:

segments.src: - **A pledge of elections.** "Elections will be held in Venezuela," she said, adding that the Venezuelan people will determine the "right moment" to move the process forward.
segments.tr: - **Uma promessa de eleições.** "Eleições serão realizadas na Venezuela," ela disse, acrescentando que o povo venezuelano determinará o "momento certo" para avançar com o processo.

segments.src: - **A dialogue with the opposition.** She said her government has begun a "political dialogue with opposition sectors" aimed at a process "based on equal conditions for all."
segments.tr: - **Um diálogo com a oposição.** Ela disse que seu governo iniciou um "diálogo político com setores da oposição" visando um processo "baseado em condições de igualdade para todos."

segments.src: - **Institutional readiness.** When a vote does take place, she said, the country's institutions "will be prepared to guarantee an inclusive and transparent process."
segments.tr: - **Prontidão institucional.** Quando uma votação realmente acontecer, ela disse, as instituições do país "estarão preparadas para garantir um processo inclusivo e transparente."

segments.src: - **A definition of democracy.** "Democracy is not measured by the mere existence of elections," she argued. It is measured, in her words, by the quality of the competition that comes before them.
segments.tr: - **Uma definição de democracia.** "A democracia não é medida pela mera existência de eleições," ela argumentou. Ela é medida, em suas palavras, pela qualidade da competição que vem antes delas.

segments.src: - **A message of renewal.** "Today, Venezuela is being reborn," she said, while cautioning, "I do not promise you an easy way forward." She described rebuilding the country's "national soul" as a priority.
segments.tr: - **Uma mensagem de renovação.** "Hoje, a Venezuela está renascendo," ela disse, ao mesmo tempo em que alertou: "Não lhes prometo um caminho fácil." Ela descreveu a reconstrução da "alma nacional" do país como uma prioridade.

segments.src: - **Thanks to Washington.** She thanked President Donald Trump and his administration for their willingness to restore diplomatic ties and described a recent meeting as "historic." She named energy, economic cooperation, security and the fight against transnational crime as areas of shared interest, and called a recent oil agreement one of the largest ever reached between the two countries.
segments.tr: - **Agradecimentos a Washington.** Ela agradeceu ao presidente Donald Trump e à sua administração pela disposição em restaurar os laços diplomáticos e descreveu uma reunião recente como "histórica." Ela citou energia, cooperação econômica, segurança e a luta contra o crime transnacional como áreas de interesse compartilhado, e chamou um recente acordo petroleiro de um dos maiores já alcançados entre os dois países.

segments.src: ## What she left out
segments.tr: ## O que ela omitiu

segments.src: Several observers noted the gaps as much as the promises.
segments.tr: Vários observadores notaram as lacunas tanto quanto as promessas.

segments.src: - **No date.** The most important detail for any election, the calendar, was absent. She offered no timeline and no benchmarks for setting one.
segments.tr: - **Sem data.** O detalhe mais importante para qualquer eleição, o calendário, esteve ausente. Ela não ofereceu cronograma nem parâmetros para estabelecer um.

segments.src: - **No named negotiating partners.** She referred to "opposition sectors" without identifying which groups are at the table.
segments.tr: - **Nenhum parceiro de negociação nomeado.** Ela se referiu a "setores da oposição" sem identificar quais grupos estão na mesa.

segments.src: - **No detail on judicial or electoral reform.** Independent analysts point out that credible elections usually depend on an updated voter roll and a restructured electoral authority. CSIS reports that no restructuring of the National Electoral Council has been discussed, and that voter rolls remain outdated.
segments.tr: - **Sem detalhes sobre reforma judicial ou eleitoral.** Analistas independentes apontam que eleições críveis geralmente dependem de um cadastro eleitoral atualizado e de uma autoridade eleitoral reestruturada. O CSIS relata que nenhuma reestruturação do Conselho Nacional Eleitoral foi discutida e que os cadastros eleitorais permanecem desatualizados.

segments.src: - **No direct response to the UN's own findings.** A UN fact-finding mission recently reported that Venezuela's repressive apparatus "remains entirely intact," and that rights violations continue despite improvements. Rodríguez's speech did not directly address that assessment.
segments.tr: - **Sem resposta direta às próprias conclusões da ONU.** Uma missão de averiguação de fatos da ONU relatou recentemente que o aparato repressivo da Venezuela "permanece inteiramente intacto" e que as violações de direitos continuam apesar das melhorias. O discurso de Rodríguez não abordou diretamente essa avaliação.

segments.src: - **No mention of Maduro by name,** according to NBC News, a notable omission given that his capture is what brought her to office.
segments.tr: - **Sem menção a Maduro pelo nome,** de acordo com a NBC News, uma omissão notável dado que sua captura foi o que a levou ao cargo.

segments.src: ## The domestic picture
segments.tr: ## O panorama interno

segments.src: The speech landed in a country still under strain.
segments.tr: O discurso repercutiu em um país ainda sob pressão.

segments.src: CSIS describes the U.S.
segments.tr: O CSIS descreve a abordagem dos EUA

segments.src: approach after January as a three-stage plan of stabilization, recovery and transition.
segments.tr: após janeiro como um plano de três estágios de estabilização, recuperação e transição.

segments.src: In its assessment, the first stage is largely complete, the second is underway but uneven, and the third, political transition, has stalled.
segments.tr: Em sua avaliação, o primeiro estágio está praticamente concluído, o segundo está em andamento, mas de forma desigual, and o terceiro, a transição política, estagnou.

segments.src: Some key data points from that analysis:
segments.tr: Alguns pontos de dados importantes dessa análise:

segments.src: - An amnesty law freed roughly one thousand detainees, but hundreds reportedly remain in custody.
segments.tr: - Uma lei de anistia libertou cerca de mil detentos, mas centenas supostamente permanecem sob custódia.

segments.src: - The U.S. eased oil-sector restrictions, opening the door to major energy investment.
segments.tr: - Os EUA flexibilizaram as restrições ao setor petrolífero, abrindo as portas para grandes investimentos em energia.

segments.src: - Ordinary Venezuelans have seen little relief. CSIS reports year-over-year inflation of about 534 percent and a frozen minimum wage that covers a tiny fraction of monthly food costs.
segments.tr: - Os venezuelanos comuns viram pouco alívio. O CSIS relata uma inflação inter anual de cerca de 534 por cento e um salário mínimo congelado que cobre uma fração minúscula dos custos mensais com alimentação.

segments.src: The opposition is also divided.
segments.tr: A oposição também está dividida.

segments.src: According to CSIS, one faction, led by Dinorah Figuera, is negotiating gradual institutional reforms.
segments.tr: De acordo com o CSIS, uma facção, liderada por Dinorah Figuera, está negociando reformas institucionais graduais.

segments.src: Another, led by María Corina Machado, who has not been able to return to Venezuela, argues that the 2024 vote already settled the question of legitimacy and is pressing for immediate presidential elections.
segments.tr: Outra, liderada por María Corina Machado, que não pôde retornar à Venezuela, argumenta que a votação de 2024 já resolveu a questão da legitimidade e está pressionando por eleições presidenciais imediatas.

segments.src: Reports say a first round of talks between the opposition and the interim government began on August 6, and a second round started on September 15.
segments.tr: Relatos dizem que uma primeira rodada de conversas entre a oposição e o governo interino começou em 6 de agosto, e uma segunda rodada começou em 15 de setembro.

segments.src: ## How Washington may respond
segments.tr: ## Como Washington pode responder

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: A posição dos EUA

segments.src: position is not a single message.
segments.tr: não é uma única mensagem.

segments.src: Reporting points to at least two currents:
segments.tr: As reportagens apontam para pelo menos duas correntes:

segments.src: 1. **The economic track.** President Trump has emphasized energy deals and normalized relations. He has also said Venezuela is "not ready yet" for elections, without offering a date. His conversation with Rodríguez was reported as warm and friendly, but also direct about the need for elections eventually.
segments.tr: 1. **A via econômica.** O presidente Trump enfatizou acordos energéticos e relações normalizadas. Ele também disse que a Venezuela "ainda não está pronta" para eleições, sem oferecer uma data. Sua conversa com Rodríguez foi relatada como calorosa e amigável, mas também direta sobre a necessidade de eleições eventualmente.

segments.src: 2. **The democratic-reform track.** Secretary of State Marco Rubio has stressed that "democratic elections are not simply about holding an election." He has cited conditions such as press freedom, freedom for all parties to organize, and reform of the electoral council. He has also suggested Venezuela's transition could move far faster than the multi-year transitions seen in Eastern Europe.
segments.tr: 2. **A via da reforma democrática.** O secretário de Estado Marco Rubio enfatizou que "eleições democráticas não tratam simplesmente de realizar uma eleição." Ele citou condições como liberdade de imprensa, liberdade para todos os partidos se organizarem e reforma do conselho eleitoral. Ele também sugeriu que a transição da Venezuela pode avançar muito mais rápido do que as transições de vários anos vistas na Europa Oriental.

segments.src: CSIS argues these mixed signals may reduce the urgency of the political transition, and it raises a sequencing question: should institutional reforms come before long-term economic agreements, or after?
segments.tr: O CSIS argumenta que esses sinais mistos podem reduzir a urgência da transição política e levanta uma questão de sequenciamento: as reformas institucionais devem vir antes dos acordos econômicos de longo prazo, ou depois?

segments.src: Supporters of the current approach say stability and investment come first.
segments.tr: Os defensores da abordagem atual dizem que a estabilidade e o investimento vêm primeiro.

segments.src: Critics worry that deals could outlast any democratic commitments.
segments.tr: Os críticos temem que os acordos possam durar mais do que quaisquer compromissos democráticos.

segments.src: ## What to watch next
segments.tr: ## O que observar a seguir

segments.src: - **An electoral calendar.** The clearest sign of progress would be a specific date or a published roadmap.
segments.tr: - **Um calendário eleitoral.** O sinal mais claro de progresso seria uma data específica ou um roteiro publicado.

segments.src: - **Electoral council reform and voter-roll updates.** These are practical prerequisites that outside observers will look for.
segments.tr: - **Reforma do conselho eleitoral e atualizações do cadastro eleitoral.** Estes são pré-requisitos práticos que os observadores externos procurarão.

segments.src: - **Outcomes from the opposition talks.** Whether the two rounds of negotiations produce written commitments, and whether the divided opposition can present a common position.
segments.tr: - **Resultados das conversas da oposição.** Se as duas rodadas de negociações produzirem compromissos por escrito, e se a oposição dividida puder apresentar uma posição comum.

segments.src: - **Prisoner releases and press freedom.** Rubio's stated conditions give Washington measurable tests to apply.
segments.tr: - **Libertação de prisioneiros e liberdade de imprensa.** As condições declaradas por Rubio dão a Washington testes mensuráveis a aplicar.

segments.src: - **U.S. policy coordination.** Whether the White House and the State Department align on how much weight to give elections relative to energy and security cooperation.
segments.tr: - **Coordenação de políticas dos EUA.** Se a Casa Branca e o Departamento de Estado se alinham sobre quanto peso dar às eleições em relação à cooperação energética e de segurança.

segments.src: ## Bottom line
segments.tr: ## Conclusão

segments.src: Rodríguez's address gave the international community a public commitment it can now refer back to: elections will be held.
segments.tr: O discurso de Rodríguez deu à comunidade internacional um compromisso público ao qual ela agora pode se referir: eleições serão realizadas.

segments.src: But a pledge without a date, a named process or concrete reforms leaves the central question open.
segments.tr: Mas uma promessa sem data, um processo nomeado ou reformas concretas deixa a questão central em aberto.

segments.src: Whether September 23 is remembered as the start of a real transition or as a carefully worded holding statement will depend on what happens in the talks, in Caracas and in Washington over the coming months.
segments.tr: Se o 23 de setembro será lembrado como o início de uma transição real ou como uma declaração de espera cuidadosamente redigida dependerá do que acontecer nas conversas, em Caracas e em Washington nos próximos meses.

segments.src: ## What she said
segments.tr: ## Apa yang dia katakan

segments.src: According to news reports, the main points of the address were:
segments.tr: Menurut laporan berita, poin-poin utama dari pidato tersebut adalah:

segments.src: - **A pledge of elections.** "Elections will be held in Venezuela," she said, adding that the Venezuelan people will determine the "right moment" to move the process forward.
segments.tr: - **Janji pemilu.** "Pemilu akan diselenggarakan di Venezuela," katanya, seraya menambahkan bahwa rakyat Venezuela akan menentukan "momen yang tepat" untuk memajukan proses tersebut.

segments.src: - **A dialogue with the opposition.** She said her government has begun a "political dialogue with opposition sectors" aimed at a process "based on equal conditions for all."
segments.tr: - **Dialog dengan oposisi.** Dia mengatakan pemerintahannya telah memulai "dialog politik dengan sektor-sektor oposisi" yang bertujuan untuk proses yang "berdasarkan kondisi yang setara bagi semua."

segments.src: - **Institutional readiness.** When a vote does take place, she said, the country's institutions "will be prepared to guarantee an inclusive and transparent process."
segments.tr: - **Kesiapan institusional.** Ketika pemungutan suara benar-benar berlangsung, katanya, institusi-institusi negara "akan siap untuk menjamin proses yang inklusif dan transparan."

segments.src: - **A definition of democracy.** "Democracy is not measured by the mere existence of elections," she argued. It is measured, in her words, by the quality of the competition that comes before them.
segments.tr: - **Definisi demokrasi.** "Demokrasi tidak diukur hanya dengan adanya pemilu," argumennya. Hal itu diukur, dalam kata-katanya, oleh kualitas persaingan yang mendahuluinya.

segments.src: - **A message of renewal.** "Today, Venezuela is being reborn," she said, while cautioning, "I do not promise you an easy way forward." She described rebuilding the country's "national soul" as a priority.
segments.tr: - **Pesan pembaruan.** "Hari ini, Venezuela sedang dilahirkan kembali," katanya, sambil memperingatkan, "Saya tidak menjanjikan jalan yang mudah ke depan." Dia menggambarkan pembangunan kembali "jiwa nasional" negara itu sebagai prioritas.

segments.src: - **Thanks to Washington.** She thanked President Donald Trump and his administration for their willingness to restore diplomatic ties and described a recent meeting as "historic." She named energy, economic cooperation, security and the fight against transnational crime as areas of shared interest, and called a recent oil agreement one of the largest ever reached between the two countries.
segments.tr: - **Terima kasih kepada Washington.** Dia berterima kasih kepada Presiden Donald Trump dan pemerintahannya atas kesediaan mereka untuk memulihkan hubungan diplomatik dan menggambarkan pertemuan baru-baru ini sebagai pertemuan yang "bersejarah." Dia menyebutkan energi, kerja sama ekonomi, keamanan, dan perang melawan kejahatan transnasional sebagai bidang-bidang yang menjadi kepentingan bersama, dan menyebut perjanjian minyak baru-baru ini sebagai salah satu yang terbesar yang pernah dicapai antara kedua negara.

segments.src: ## What she left out
segments.tr: ## Apa yang dia lewatkan

segments.src: Several observers noted the gaps as much as the promises.
segments.tr: Beberapa pengamat mencatat kesenjangan tersebut sama besarnya dengan janji-janji yang diberikan.

segments.src: - **No date.** The most important detail for any election, the calendar, was absent. She offered no timeline and no benchmarks for setting one.
segments.tr: - **Tidak ada tanggal.** Rincian paling penting untuk pemilu apa pun, yaitu kalender, tidak ada. Dia tidak menawarkan garis waktu dan tidak ada tolok ukur untuk menetapkannya.

segments.src: - **No named negotiating partners.** She referred to "opposition sectors" without identifying which groups are at the table.
segments.tr: - **Tidak ada mitra negosiasi yang disebutkan namanya.** Dia merujuk pada "sektor oposisi" tanpa mengidentifikasi kelompok mana yang berada di meja perundingan.

segments.src: - **No detail on judicial or electoral reform.** Independent analysts point out that credible elections usually depend on an updated voter roll and a restructured electoral authority. CSIS reports that no restructuring of the National Electoral Council has been discussed, and that voter rolls remain outdated.
segments.tr: - **Tidak ada rincian tentang reformasi peradilan atau pemilu.** Analis independen menunjukkan bahwa pemilu yang kredibel biasanya bergantung pada daftar pemilih yang diperbarui dan otoritas pemilu yang direstrukturisasi. CSIS melaporkan bahwa tidak ada restrukturisasi Dewan Pemilihan Nasional yang telah dibahas, dan daftar pemilih tetap usang.

segments.src: - **No direct response to the UN's own findings.** A UN fact-finding mission recently reported that Venezuela's repressive apparatus "remains entirely intact," and that rights violations continue despite improvements. Rodríguez's speech did not directly address that assessment.
segments.tr: - **Tidak ada tanggapan langsung terhadap temuan PBB sendiri.** Misi pencari fakta PBB baru-baru ini melaporkan bahwa aparat represif Venezuela "tetap utuh sepenuhnya," dan bahwa pelanggaran hak asasi manusia terus berlanjut meskipun ada perbaikan. Pidato Rodríguez tidak secara langsung menanggapi penilaian tersebut.

segments.src: - **No mention of Maduro by name,** according to NBC News, a notable omission given that his capture is what brought her to office.
segments.tr: - **Tidak ada penyebutan nama Maduro,** menurut NBC News, sebuah kelalaian yang mencolok mengingat penangkapannya adalah hal yang membawanya ke tampuk kekuasaan.

segments.src: - Ordinary Venezuelans have seen little relief. CSIS reports year-over-year inflation of about 534 percent and a frozen minimum wage that covers a tiny fraction of monthly food costs.
segments.tr: - Rakyat Venezuela biasa hanya melihat sedikit kelegaan. CSIS melaporkan inflasi tahun-ke-tahun sekitar 534 persen dan upah minimum yang dibekukan yang hanya mencakup sebagian kecil dari biaya makanan bulanan.

segments.src: The opposition is also divided.
segments.tr: Oposisi juga terpecah.

segments.src: According to CSIS, one faction, led by Dinorah Figuera, is negotiating gradual institutional reforms.
segments.tr: Menurut CSIS, satu faksi, yang dipimpin oleh Dinorah Figuera, sedang menegosiasikan reformasi institusional secara bertahap.

segments.src: Another, led by María Corina Machado, who has not been able to return to Venezuela, argues that the 2024 vote already settled the question of legitimacy and is pressing for immediate presidential elections.
segments.tr: Faksi lain, yang dipimpin oleh María Corina Machado, yang belum dapat kembali ke Venezuela, berargumen bahwa pemungutan suara tahun 2024 telah menyelesaikan masalah legitimasi dan mendesak diadakannya pemilihan presiden segera.

segments.src: Reports say a first round of talks between the opposition and the interim government began on August 6, and a second round started on September 15.
segments.tr: Laporan-laporan mengatakan putaran pertama pembicaraan antara oposisi dan pemerintah interim dimulai pada tanggal 6 Agustus, dan putaran kedua dimulai pada tanggal 15 September.

segments.src: ## How Washington may respond
segments.tr: ## Bagaimana Washington mungkin merespons

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: Posisi AS

segments.src: position is not a single message.
segments.tr: bukanlah pesan tunggal.

segments.src: Reporting points to at least two currents:
segments.tr: Laporan menunjukkan setidaknya ada dua arus:

segments.src: 1. **The economic track.** President Trump has emphasized energy deals and normalized relations. He has also said Venezuela is "not ready yet" for elections, without offering a date. His conversation with Rodríguez was reported as warm and friendly, but also direct about the need for elections eventually.
segments.tr: 1. **Jalur ekonomi.** Presiden Trump telah menekankan kesepakatan energi dan normalisasi hubungan. Dia juga mengatakan Venezuela "belum siap" untuk pemilu, tanpa menawarkan tanggal. Percakapannya dengan Rodríguez dilaporkan hangat dan bersahabat, tetapi juga langsung mengenai perlunya pemilu pada akhirnya.

segments.src: 2. **The democratic-reform track.** Secretary of State Marco Rubio has stressed that "democratic elections are not simply about holding an election." He has cited conditions such as press freedom, freedom for all parties to organize, and reform of the electoral council. He has also suggested Venezuela's transition could move far faster than the multi-year transitions seen in Eastern Europe.
segments.tr: 2. **Jalur reformasi demokratis.** Menteri Luar Negeri Marco Rubio telah menekankan bahwa "pemilu demokratis bukan sekadar tentang menyelenggarakan pemilu." Dia mengutip kondisi-kondisi seperti kebebasan pers, kebebasan bagi semua partai untuk berorganisasi, dan reformasi dewan pemilihan. Dia juga menyarankan transisi Venezuela dapat bergerak jauh lebih cepat daripada transisi multi-tahun yang terlihat di Eropa Timur.

segments.src: CSIS argues these mixed signals may reduce the urgency of the political transition, and it raises a sequencing question: should institutional reforms come before long-term economic agreements, or after?
segments.tr: CSIS berargumen bahwa sinyal-sinyal beragam ini dapat mengurangi urgensi transisi politik, dan hal ini menimbulkan pertanyaan tentang urutan: haruskah reformasi institusional dilakukan sebelum perjanjian ekonomi jangka panjang, atau sesudahnya?

segments.src: Supporters of the current approach say stability and investment come first.
segments.tr: Pendukung pendekatan saat ini mengatakan stabilitas dan investasi adalah yang utama.

segments.src: Critics worry that deals could outlast any democratic commitments.
segments.tr: Kritikus khawatir bahwa kesepakatan-kesepakatan tersebut dapat bertahan lebih lama daripada komitmen demokratis apa pun.

segments.src: ## What to watch next
segments.tr: ## Apa yang harus diperhatikan selanjutnya

segments.src: - **An electoral calendar.** The clearest sign of progress would be a specific date or a published roadmap.
segments.tr: - **Kalender pemilu.** Tanda kemajuan yang paling jelas adalah tanggal spesifik atau peta jalan yang dipublikasikan.

segments.src: - **Electoral council reform and voter-roll updates.** These are practical prerequisites that outside observers will look for.
segments.tr: - **Reformasi dewan pemilihan dan pembaruan daftar pemilih.** Ini adalah prasyarat praktis yang akan dicari oleh pengamat luar.

segments.src: - **Outcomes from the opposition talks.** Whether the two rounds of negotiations produce written commitments, and whether the divided opposition can present a common position.
segments.tr: - **Hasil dari pembicaraan oposisi.** Apakah kedua putaran negosiasi menghasilkan komitmen tertulis, dan apakah oposisi yang terpecah dapat menyajikan posisi bersama.

segments.src: - **Prisoner releases and press freedom.** Rubio's stated conditions give Washington measurable tests to apply.
segments.tr: - **Pembebasan tahanan dan kebebasan pers.** Kondisi yang dinyatakan Rubio memberi Washington ujian terukur untuk diterapkan.

segments.src: - **U.S. policy coordination.** Whether the White House and the State Department align on how much weight to give elections relative to energy and security cooperation.
segments.tr: - **Koordinasi kebijakan AS.** Apakah Gedung Putih dan Departemen Luar Negeri menyelaraskan seberapa besar bobot yang diberikan pada pemilu relatif terhadap kerja sama energi dan keamanan.

segments.src: ## Bottom line
segments.tr: ## Intinya

segments.src: Rodríguez's address gave the international community a public commitment it can now refer back to: elections will be held.
segments.tr: Pidato Rodríguez memberi komunitas internasional komitmen publik yang kini dapat dirujuk kembali: pemilu akan diselenggarakan.

segments.src: But a pledge without a date, a named process or concrete reforms leaves the central question open.
segments.tr: Namun, janji tanpa tanggal, proses yang jelas, atau reformasi konkret membiarkan pertanyaan sentral tetap terbuka.

segments.src: Whether September 23 is remembered as the start of a real transition or as a carefully worded holding statement will depend on what happens in the talks, in Caracas and in Washington over the coming months.
segments.tr: Apakah tanggal 23 September akan diingat sebagai awal dari transisi nyata atau sebagai pernyataan penahanan yang dirumuskan dengan hati-hati akan bergantung pada apa yang terjadi dalam pembicaraan di Caracas dan di Washington selama bulan-bulan mendatang.

ja.title: 「選挙が実施される」：デルシー・ロドリゲスの初国連演説が明かす、マドゥロ後ベネズエラの行く末

segments.src: Venezuela's acting president, Delcy Rodríguez, took the podium at the United Nations General Assembly on September 23, 2026, and told world leaders that "elections will be held in Venezuela."
segments.tr: ベネズエラのデルシー・ロドリゲス大統領代行は、2026年9月23日に国連総会で演壇に立ち、世界の指導者らに対して「ベネズエラで選挙が実施される」と述べた。

segments.src: What she did not say was when.
segments.tr: 彼女が言わなかったのは、それがいつかということだった。

segments.src: Nearly nine months after U.S.
segments.tr: 米国がニコラス・マドゥロを拘束してから約9ヶ月後、

segments.src: forces captured Nicolás Maduro in January, the speech offered a promise, a tone of reconciliation with Washington, and very few specifics.
segments.tr: 1月のこの演説は、公約と、ワシントンとの和解のトーン、そして非常に少ない具体策を提示した。

segments.src: This explainer covers what she said, what was missing, and how the United States and Venezuela's opposition may respond, based on reporting from NBC News, NPR, UPI and analysis from the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS).
segments.tr: この解説記事では、NBC News、NPR、UPIの報道および戦略国際問題研究所（CSIS）の分析に基づき、彼女の発言内容、欠けていた点、そして米国およびベネズエラ野党がどのように対応する可能性があるかを取り上げる。

segments.src: ## Why this speech matters
segments.tr: ## なぜこの演説が重要なのか

segments.src: Rodríguez's appearance carried symbolic weight before she said a word.
segments.tr: ロドリゲスの登場は、一言もしゃべる前から象徴的な重みを持っていた。

segments.src: Reports describe it as the first visit to the United States by a Venezuelan head of state since 2018, when Maduro himself traveled to New York for the General Assembly.
segments.tr: 報道によると、これは2018年にマドゥロ自身が総会のためにニューヨークを訪れて以来、ベネズエラ元首による米国への初めての訪問とされている。

segments.src: She took over after a surprise U.S.
segments.tr: 彼女は、1月の米国の突然の軍事作戦によりマドゥロが拘束され、麻薬密輸の罪に問うために米国へ連行された後に政権を引き継いだ。

segments.src: military operation in January that captured Maduro and brought him to the United States to face drug trafficking charges.
Since then, her government and Washington have moved from confrontation toward a working, if uneasy, relationship.
segments.tr: それ以来、彼女の政府とワシントンは対決から、ぎこちないながらも実務的な関係へと移行してきた。

segments.src: Standing at the UN lectern, Rodríguez was presenting Venezuela's new chapter to the world for the first time.
segments.tr: 国連の演壇に立ち、ロドリゲスはベネズエラの新しい章を世界に向けて初めて提示していた。

segments.src: ## What she said
segments.tr: ## 彼女の発言内容

segments.src: According to news reports, the main points of the address were:
segments.tr: 報道によると、演説の主なポイントは以下の通りである：

segments.src: - **A pledge of elections.** "Elections will be held in Venezuela," she said, adding that the Venezuelan people will determine the "right moment" to move the process forward.
segments.tr: - **選挙の公約。**「ベネズエラで選挙が実施される」と彼女は述べ、ベネズエラ国民がプロセスを進める「適切な瞬間」を決定すると付け加えた。

segments.src: - **A dialogue with the opposition.** She said her government has begun a "political dialogue with opposition sectors" aimed at a process "based on equal conditions for all."
segments.tr: - **野党との対話。**彼女は、政府が「全員に平等な条件に基づく」プロセスを目指して、「野党勢力との政治対話」を開始したと述べた。

segments.src: - **Institutional readiness.** When a vote does take place, she said, the country's institutions "will be prepared to guarantee an inclusive and transparent process."
segments.tr: - **制度的準備。**投票が実際に実施される際、国の制度は「包括的で透明なプロセスを保証するための準備ができるだろう」と彼女は述べた。

segments.src: - **A definition of democracy.** "Democracy is not measured by the mere existence of elections," she argued. It is measured, in her words, by the quality of the competition that comes before them.
segments.tr: - **民主主義の定義。**「民主主義は単なる選挙の存在によって測られるものではない」と彼女は主張した。それは、彼女の言葉によれば、その前に行われる競争の質によって測られる。

segments.src: - **A message of renewal.** "Today, Venezuela is being reborn," she said, while cautioning, "I do not promise you an easy way forward." She described rebuilding the country's "national soul" as a priority.
segments.tr: - **刷新のメッセージ。**「今日、ベネズエラは生まれ変わりつつある」と彼女は述べた一方で、「平坦な道のりであるとは約束しない」と警告した。彼女は国の「国民的魂」の再建を優先事項として描いた。

segments.src: - **Thanks to Washington.** She thanked President Donald Trump and his administration for their willingness to restore diplomatic ties and described a recent meeting as "historic." She named energy, economic cooperation, security and the fight against transnational crime as areas of shared interest, and called a recent oil agreement one of the largest ever reached between the two countries.
segments.tr: - **ワシントンへの感謝。**彼女はドナルド・トランプ大統領と彼の政権の外交関係修復への意欲に感謝し、最近の会談を「歴史的」と表現した。彼女はエネルギー、経済協力、安全保障、および国際犯罪との戦いを共通の関心分野として挙げ、最近の石油合意を両国間でこれまでに締結された最大の合意の一つと呼んだ。

segments.src: ## What she left out
segments.tr: ## 彼女が省いたもの

segments.src: Several observers noted the gaps as much as the promises.
segments.tr: 複数の観察者が、公約と同様にその空白部分についても指摘した。

segments.src: - **No date.** The most important detail for any election, the calendar, was absent. She offered no timeline and no benchmarks for setting one.
segments.tr: - **期日の不在。**いかなる選挙にとっても最も重要な詳細であるカレンダーが欠如していた。彼女はタイムラインも、それを設定するためのベンチマークも提示しなかった。

segments.src: - **No named negotiating partners.** She referred to "opposition sectors" without identifying which groups are at the table.
segments.tr: - **名指しされなかった交渉相手。**彼女はどのグループが交渉のテーブルについているのかを特定することなく、「野党勢力」言及した。

segments.src: - **No detail on judicial or electoral reform.** Independent analysts point out that credible elections usually depend on an updated voter roll and a restructured electoral authority. CSIS reports that no restructuring of the National Electoral Council has been discussed, and that voter rolls remain outdated.
segments.tr: - **司法または選挙改革に関する詳細の欠如。**独立系アナリストは、信頼できる選挙は通常、更新された有権者名簿と再編された選挙管理機関に依存すると指摘している。CSISの報道によれば、国家選挙評議会の再編について議論されたことはなく、有権者名簿は古いままとなっている。

segments.src: - **No direct response to the UN's own findings.** A UN fact-finding mission recently reported that Venezuela's repressive apparatus "remains entirely intact," and that rights violations continue despite improvements. Rodríguez's speech did not directly address that assessment.
segments.tr: - **国連自体の調査結果に対する直接的な言答の不在。**国連の事実調査団は最近、ベネズエラの弾圧機構が「完全にそのまま残っており」、改善が見られるにもかかわらず権利侵害が続いていると報告した。ロドリゲスの演説はその評価に直接言及しなかった。

segments.src: - **No mention of Maduro by name,** according to NBC News, a notable omission given that his capture is what brought her to office.
segments.tr: - **NBC Newsによると、マドゥロの名前についての言及がないこと。**彼の拘束が彼女を就任させたきっかけであることを考えると、これは特筆すべき省略である。

segments.src: ## The domestic picture
segments.tr: ## 国内の状況

segments.src: The speech landed in a country still under strain.
segments.tr: この演説は、依然として緊張下にある国で行われた。

segments.src: CSIS describes the U.S.
segments.tr: CSISは1月以降の米国の

segments.src: approach after January as a three-stage plan of stabilization, recovery and transition.
segments.tr: アプローチを、安定化、回復、移行の3段階の計画として描写している。

segments.src: In its assessment, the first stage is largely complete, the second is underway but uneven, and the third, political transition, has stalled.
segments.tr: その評価では、第1段階は概ね完了し、第2段階は進行中だが不均等であり、第3段階の政治的移行は停滞している。

segments.src: Some key data points from that analysis:
segments.tr: その分析からのいくつかの重要なデータポイント：

segments.src: - An amnesty law freed roughly one thousand detainees, but hundreds reportedly remain in custody.
segments.tr: - 恩赦法により約1000人の拘留者が釈放されたが、数百人が依然として勾留されていると報じられている。

segments.src: - The U.S. eased oil-sector restrictions, opening the door to major energy investment.
segments.tr: - 米国は石油部門の制限を緩和し、大規模なエネルギー投資への扉を開いた。

segments.src: - Ordinary Venezuelans have seen little relief. CSIS reports year-over-year inflation of about 534 percent and a frozen minimum wage that covers a tiny fraction of monthly food costs.
segments.tr: - 一般のベネズエラ人はほとんど救済を受けていない。CSISは、前年比のインフレ率が約534パーセントであり、月々の食費のほんの一部しかカバーしない凍結された最低賃金を報告している。

segments.src: The opposition is also divided.
segments.tr: 野党もまた分裂している。

segments.src: According to CSIS, one faction, led by Dinorah Figuera, is negotiating gradual institutional reforms.
segments.tr: CSISによると、ディノラ・フィゲラが率いる一派は段階的な制度改革を交渉している。

segments.src: Another, led by María Corina Machado, who has not been able to return to Venezuela, argues that the 2024 vote already settled the question of legitimacy and is pressing for immediate presidential elections.
segments.tr: ベネズエラに戻ることができていないマリア・コリナ・マチャドが率いるもう一つの派閥は、2024年の投票ですでに正統性の問題が解決されたと主張し、即時大統領選挙を求めている。

segments.src: Reports say a first round of talks between the opposition and the interim government began on August 6, and a second round started on September 15.
segments.tr: 報道によると、野党と暫定政府の間の最初の協議ラウンドは8月6日に始まり、第2ラウンドは9月15日に始まった。

segments.src: ## How Washington may respond
segments.tr: ## ワシントンはどのように対応する可能性があるか

segments.src: Reporting points to at least two currents:
segments.tr: 報道は少なくとも2つの流れを指摘している：

segments.src: 1. **The economic track.** President Trump has emphasized energy deals and normalized relations. He has also said Venezuela is "not ready yet" for elections, without offering a date. His conversation with Rodríguez was reported as warm and friendly, but also direct about the need for elections eventually.

He has cited conditions such as press freedom, freedom for all parties to organize, and reform of the electoral council. segments.src: Supporters of the current approach say stability and investment come first.

segments.src: ## What to watch next

segments.src: ## Bottom line
segments.tr: ## 結論

segments.src: Rodríguez's address gave the international community a public commitment it can now refer back to: elections will be held.
segments.tr: ロドリゲスの演説は、国際社会が今後振り返ることができる公のコミットメントを与えた：選挙が実施されるということだ。

de.title: "Wahlen werden stattfinden": Was Delcy Rodríguez' erste UN-Rede über Venezuelas Weg nach Maduro verrät

segments.src: Venezuela's acting president, Delcy Rodríguez, took the podium at the United Nations General Assembly on September 23, 2026, and told world leaders that "elections will be held in Venezuela."
segments.tr: Die kommissarische Präsidentin Venezuelas, Delcy Rodríguez, trat am 23. September 2026 ans Rednerpult der Generalversammlung der Vereinten Nationen und erklärte den Staats- und Regierungschefs der Welt, dass „in Venezuela Wahlen stattfinden werden“.

segments.src: What she did not say was when.
segments.tr: Was sie jedoch nicht sagte, war wann.

segments.src: Nearly nine months after U.S.
segments.tr: Knapp neun Monate nach den US-

segments.src: forces captured Nicolás Maduro in January, the speech offered a promise, a tone of reconciliation with Washington, and very few specifics.
segments.tr: Streitkräften, die Nicolás Maduro im Januar festgenommen hatten, bot die Rede ein Versprechen, einen Ton der Versöhnung mit Washington und nur sehr wenige konkrete Details.

segments.src: This explainer covers what she said, what was missing, and how the United States and Venezuela's opposition may respond, based on reporting from NBC News, NPR, UPI and analysis from the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS).
segments.tr: Dieser Erklärbeitrag beleuchtet, was sie sagte, was fehlte und wie die Vereinigten Staaten und Venezuelas Opposition darauf reagieren könnten, basierend auf Berichten von NBC News, NPR, UPI und Analysen des Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS).

segments.src: ## Why this speech matters
segments.tr: ## Warum diese Rede wichtig ist

segments.src: Rodríguez's appearance carried symbolic weight before she said a word.
segments.tr: Rodríguez' Auftritt hatte bereits symbolisches Gewicht, bevor sie ein einziges Wort sprach.

segments.src: Reports describe it as the first visit to the United States by a Venezuelan head of state since 2018, when Maduro himself traveled to New York for the General Assembly.
segments.tr: Berichten zufolge handelt es sich dabei um den ersten Besuch eines venezolanischen Staatsoberhaupts in den Vereinigten Staaten seit 2018, als Maduro selbst zur Generalversammlung nach New York gereist war.

segments.src: She took over after a surprise U.S.
segments.tr: Sie übernahm die Macht nach einer überraschenden US-

segments.src: military operation in January that captured Maduro and brought him to the United States to face drug trafficking charges.
segments.tr: Militäroperation im Januar, bei der Maduro festgenommen und in die Vereinigten Staaten gebracht wurde, um sich dort wegen Drogenhandelsvorwürfen zu verantworten.

segments.src: Since then, her government and Washington have moved from confrontation toward a working, if uneasy, relationship.
segments.tr: Seitdem hat sich ihre Regierung von der Konfrontation auf eine arbeitsfähige, wenn auch unangenehme Beziehung zu Washington zubewegt.

segments.src: Standing at the UN lectern, Rodríguez was presenting Venezuela's new chapter to the world for the first time.
segments.tr: Am UN-Rednerpult stehend präsentierte Rodríguez der Welt zum ersten Mal das neue Kapitel Venezuelas.

segments.src: ## What she said
segments.tr: ## Was sie sagte

segments.src: According to news reports, the main points of the address were:
segments.tr: Berichten zufolge waren die Hauptpunkte der Ansprache:

segments.src: - **A pledge of elections.** "Elections will be held in Venezuela," she said, adding that the Venezuelan people will determine the "right moment" to move the process forward.
segments.tr: - **Ein Versprechen von Wahlen.** „Wahlen werden in Venezuela stattfinden“, sagte sie und fügte hinzu, das venezolanische Volk werde den „richtigen Moment“ bestimmen, um den Prozess voranzutreiben.

segments.src: - **A dialogue with the opposition.** She said her government has begun a "political dialogue with opposition sectors" aimed at a process "based on equal conditions for all."
segments.tr: - **Ein Dialog mit der Opposition.** Sie sagte, ihre Regierung habe einen „politischen Dialog mit Oppositionskreisen“ begonnen, der auf einen Prozess „auf der Grundlage gleicher Bedingungen für alle“ abzielt.

segments.src: - **Institutional readiness.** When a vote does take place, she said, the country's institutions "will be prepared to guarantee an inclusive and transparent process."
segments.tr: - **Institutionelle Bereitschaft.** Wenn eine Abstimmung stattfinde, seien die Institutionen des Landes „bereit, einen inklusiven und transparenten Prozess zu garantieren“, sagte sie.

segments.src: - **A definition of democracy.** "Democracy is not measured by the mere existence of elections," she argued. It is measured, in her words, by the quality of the competition that comes before them.
segments.tr: - **Eine Definition von Demokratie.** „Demokratie bemisst sich nicht nach dem bloßen Vorhandensein von Wahlen“, argumentierte sie. Sie bemesse sich, ihren Worten nach, an der Qualität des Wettbewerbs, der ihnen vorausgeht.

segments.src: - **A message of renewal.** "Today, Venezuela is being reborn," she said, while cautioning, "I do not promise you an easy way forward." She described rebuilding the country's "national soul" as a priority.
segments.tr: - **Eine Botschaft der Erneuerung.** „Heute wird Venezuela wiedergeboren“, sagte sie und warnte zugleich: „Ich verspreche Ihnen keinen leichten Weg nach vorn.“ Sie bezeichnete den Wiederaufbau der „nationalen Seele“ des Landes als Priorität.

segments.src: - **Thanks to Washington.** She thanked President Donald Trump and his administration for their willingness to restore diplomatic ties and described a recent meeting as "historic." She named energy, economic cooperation, security and the fight against transnational crime as areas of shared interest, and called a recent oil agreement one of the largest ever reached between the two countries.
segments.tr: - **Dank an Washington.** Sie dankte Präsident Donald Trump und seiner Regierung für deren Bereitschaft, die diplomatischen Beziehungen wiederherzustellen, und bezeichnete ein kürzliches Treffen als „historisch“. Sie nannte Energie, wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit, Sicherheit und den Kampf gegen grenzüberschreitende Kriminalität als Bereiche von gemeinsames Interesse und bezeichnete ein kürzlich geschlossenes Erdölabkommen als eines der größten, die jemals zwischen den beiden Ländern erzielt wurden.

segments.src: ## What she left out
segments.tr: ## Was sie ausließ

segments.src: Several observers noted the gaps as much as the promises.
segments.tr: Mehrere Beobachter wiesen ebenso auf die Lücken wie auf die Versprechen hin.

segments.src: - **No date.** The most important detail for any election, the calendar, was absent. She offered no timeline and no benchmarks for setting one.
segments.tr: - **Kein Datum.** Das wichtigste Detail für jede Wahl, der Kalender, fehlte. Sie nannte keinen Zeitplan und keine Maßstäbe für dessen Festlegung.

segments.src: - **No named negotiating partners.** She referred to "opposition sectors" without identifying which groups are at the table.
segments.tr: - **Keine benannten Verhandlungspartner.** Sie bezog sich auf „Oppositionskreise“, ohne zu benennen, welche Gruppen am Tisch sitzen.

segments.src: - **No detail on judicial or electoral reform.** Independent analysts point out that credible elections usually depend on an updated voter roll and a restructured electoral authority. CSIS reports that no restructuring of the National Electoral Council has been discussed, and that voter rolls remain outdated.
segments.tr: - **Keine Details zu Justiz- oder Wahlreformen.** Unabhängige Analysten weisen darauf hin, dass glaubwürdige Wahlen in der Regel von einem aktualisierten Wählerverzeichnis und einer umstrukturierten Wahlbehörde abhängen. CSIS-Berichten zufolge wurde über keine Umstrukturierung des Nationalen Wahlrates diskutiert und die Wählerverzeichnisse seien veraltet.

segments.src: - **No direct response to the UN's own findings.** A UN fact-finding mission recently reported that Venezuela's repressive apparatus "remains entirely intact," and that rights violations continue despite improvements. Rodríguez's speech did not directly address that assessment.
segments.tr: - **Keine direkte Reaktion auf die eigenen Erkenntnisse der UN.** Eine UN-Untersuchungskommission berichtete kürzlich, dass Venezuelas repressiver Apparat „vollständig intakt bleibt“ und die Menschenrechtsverletzungen trotz Verbesserungen anhalten. Rodríguez' Rede ging auf diese Einschätzung nicht direkt ein.

segments.src: - **No mention of Maduro by name,** according to NBC News, a notable omission given that his capture is what brought her to office.
segments.tr: - **Keine namentliche Erwähnung von Maduro,** so NBC News – eine bemerkenswerte Auslassung angesichts der Tatsache, dass seine Festnahme sie erst ins Amt gebracht hat.

segments.src: ## The domestic picture
segments.tr: ## Das Bild im Inland

segments.src: The speech landed in a country still under strain.
segments.tr: Die Rede fiel in ein Land, das nach wie vor unter Druck steht.

segments.src: CSIS describes the U.S.
segments.tr: CSIS beschreibt das US-

segments.src: approach after January as a three-stage plan of stabilization, recovery and transition.
segments.tr: Vorgehen nach dem Januar als einen dreistufigen Plan aus Stabilisierung, Erholung und Übergang.

segments.src: In its assessment, the first stage is largely complete, the second is underway but uneven, and the third, political transition, has stalled.
segments.tr: Ihrer Einschätzung nach ist die erste Phase weitgehend abgeschlossen, die zweite im Gange, aber ungleichmäßig, und die dritte, der politische Übergang, ins Stocken geraten.

segments.src: Some key data points from that analysis:
segments.tr: Einige wichtige Datenpunkte aus dieser Analyse:

segments.src: - An amnesty law freed roughly one thousand detainees, but hundreds reportedly remain in custody.
segments.tr: - Ein Amnestiegesetz ließ rund tausend Häftlinge frei, doch Berichten zufolge befinden sich Hunderte weiterhin in Haft.

segments.src: - The U.S. eased oil-sector restrictions, opening the door to major energy investment.
segments.tr: - Die USA lockerten die Beschränkungen für den Ölsektor und öffneten damit die Tür für größere Energieinvestitionen.

segments.src: - Ordinary Venezuelans have seen little relief. CSIS reports year-over-year inflation of about 534 percent and a frozen minimum wage that covers a tiny fraction of monthly food costs.
segments.tr: - Gewöhnliche Venezolaner haben kaum Entlastung erfahren. CSIS berichtet von einer Inflation von etwa 534 Prozent im Jahresvergleich und einem eingefrorenen Mindestlohn, der nur einen Bruchteil der monatlichen Kosten für Lebensmittel deckt.

segments.src: The opposition is also divided.
segments.tr: Auch die Opposition ist gespalten.

segments.src: According to CSIS, one faction, led by Dinorah Figuera, is negotiating gradual institutional reforms.
segments.tr: Dem CSIS zufolge verhandelt eine von Dinorah Figuera angeführte Fraktion über schrittuelle institutionelle Reformen.

segments.src: Another, led by María Corina Machado, who has not been able to return to Venezuela, argues that the 2024 vote already settled the question of legitimacy and is pressing for immediate presidential elections.
segments.tr: Eine andere, angeführt von María Corina Machado, die nicht nach Venezuela zurückkehren konnte, argumentiert, dass die Abstimmung von 2024 die Frage der Legitimität bereits geklärt habe, und drängt auf sofortige Präsidentschaftswahlen.

segments.src: Reports say a first round of talks between the opposition and the interim government began on August 6, and a second round started on September 15.
segments.tr: Berichten zufolge begann eine erste Runde von Gesprächen zwischen der Opposition und der Übergangsregierung am 6. August, und eine zweite Runde startete am 15. September.

segments.src: ## How Washington may respond
segments.tr: ## Wie Washington reagieren könnte

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: Die US-

segments.src: position is not a single message.
segments.tr: Position ist keine einheitliche Botschaft.

segments.src: Reporting points to at least two currents:
segments.tr: Berichte deuten auf mindestens zwei Strömungen hin:

segments.src: 1. **The economic track.** President Trump has emphasized energy deals and normalized relations. He has also said Venezuela is "not ready yet" for elections, without offering a date. His conversation with Rodríguez was reported as warm and friendly, but also direct about the need for elections eventually.
segments.tr: 1. **Die wirtschaftliche Schiene.** Präsident Trump hat Energieabkommen und normalisierte Beziehungen betont. Er hat außerdem gesagt, Venezuela sei für Wahlen „noch nicht bereit“, ohne ein Datum zu nennen. Sein Gespräch mit Rodríguez wurde als herzlich und freundlich beschrieben, aber auch direkt bezüglich der Notwendigkeit von Wahlen zu gegebener Zeit.

segments.src: 2. **The democratic-reform track.** Secretary of State Marco Rubio has stressed that "democratic elections are not simply about holding an election." He has cited conditions such as press freedom, freedom for all parties to organize, and reform of the electoral council. He has also suggested Venezuela's transition could move far faster than the multi-year transitions seen in Eastern Europe.
segments.tr: 2. **Die Schiene der demokratischen Reformen.** Außenminister Marco Rubio hat betont, dass „demokratische Wahlen nicht einfach nur darin bestehen, eine Wahl abzuhalten“. Er nannte Bedingungen wie Pressefreiheit, Freiheit für alle Parteien zur Organisation und Reform des Wahlrates. Er hat auch angedeutet, dass der Übergang Venezuelas weitaus schneller verlaufen könnte als die mehrjährigen Übergänge in Osteuropa.

segments.src: CSIS argues these mixed signals may reduce the urgency of the political transition, and it raises a sequencing question: should institutional reforms come before long-term economic agreements, or after?
segments.tr: CSIS argumentiert, dass diese gemischten Signale die Dringlichkeit des politischen Übergangs verringern könnten, und wirft eine Sequenzierungsfrage auf: Sollten institutionelle Reformen vor langfristigen Wirtschaftsvereinbarungen stattfinden oder danach?

segments.src: Supporters of the current approach say stability and investment come first.
segments.tr: Befürworter des aktuellen Ansatzes sagen, Stabilität und Investitionen stünden an erster Stelle.

segments.src: Critics worry that deals could outlast any democratic commitments.
segments.tr: Kritiker befürchten, dass Abkommen jegliche demokratischen Verpflichtungen überdauern könnten.

segments.src: ## What to watch next
segments.tr: ## Worauf als Nächstes zu achten ist

segments.src: - **An electoral calendar.** The clearest sign of progress would be a specific date or a published roadmap.
segments.tr: - **Ein Wahlkalender.** Das klarste Zeichen für Fortschritte wäre ein konkretes Datum oder eine veröffentlichte Roadmap.

segments.src: - **Electoral council reform and voter-roll updates.** These are practical prerequisites that outside observers will look for.
segments.tr: - **Reform des Wahlrates und Aktualisierung der Wählerverzeichnisse.** Dies sind praktische Voraussetzungen, nach denen externe Beobachter Ausschau halten werden.

segments.src: - **Outcomes from the opposition talks.** Whether the two rounds of negotiations produce written commitments, and whether the divided opposition can present a common position.
segments.tr: - **Ergebnisse der Oppositionsgespräche.** Ob die beiden Verhandlungsrunden schriftliche Zusagen hervorbringen und ob die gespaltene Opposition eine gemeinsame Position präsentieren kann.

segments.src: - **Prisoner releases and press freedom.** Rubio's stated conditions give Washington measurable tests to apply.
segments.tr: - **Gefangenenfreilassungen und Pressefreiheit.** Rubios genannte Bedingungen geben Washington messbare Tests an die Hand.

segments.src: - **U.S. policy coordination.** Whether the White House and the State Department align on how much weight to give elections relative to energy and security cooperation.
segments.tr: - **Koordination der US-Politik.** Ob das Weiße Haus und das Außenministerium sich darüber abstimmen, wie viel Gewicht Wahlen im Vergleich zur Energie- und Sicherheitskooperation eingeräumt werden soll.

segments.src: ## Bottom line
segments.tr: ## Fazit

segments.src: Rodríguez's address gave the international community a public commitment it can now refer back to: elections will be held.
segments.tr: Rodríguez' Ansprache gab der internationalen Gemeinschaft eine öffentliche Selbstverpflichtung, auf die sie sich nun berufen kann: Wahlen werden stattfinden.

segments.src: But a pledge without a date, a named process or concrete reforms leaves the central question open.
segments.tr: Aber ein Versprechen ohne Datum, benannten Prozess oder konkrete Reformen lässt die zentrale Frage offen.

segments.src: Whether September 23 is remembered as the start of a real transition or as a carefully worded holding statement will depend on what happens in the talks, in Caracas and in Washington over the coming months.
segments.tr: Ob der 23. September als Startpunkt eines echten Übergangs oder als sorgfältig formulierte Hinhalteerklärung in Erinnerung bleiben wird, hängt davon ab, was in den kommenden Monaten in den Gesprächen, in Caracas und in Washington passiert.

segments.src: ## What she said
segments.tr: ## Những gì bà đã nói

segments.src: According to news reports, the main points of the address were:
segments.tr: Theo các báo cáo tin tức, các điểm chính của bài phát biểu là:

segments.src: - **A pledge of elections.** "Elections will be held in Venezuela," she said, adding that the Venezuelan people will determine the "right moment" to move the process forward.
segments.tr: - **Một cam kết bầu cử.** "Bầu cử sẽ được tổ chức tại Venezuela," bà nói, đồng thời cho biết thêm rằng người dân Venezuela sẽ quyết định "thời điểm thích hợp" để thúc đẩy tiến trình này.

segments.src: - **A dialogue with the opposition.** She said her government has begun a "political dialogue with opposition sectors" aimed at a process "based on equal conditions for all."
segments.tr: - **Một cuộc đối thoại với phe đối lập.** Bà cho biết chính phủ của mình đã bắt đầu một "cuộc đối thoại chính trị với các thành phần đối lập" nhằm hướng tới một tiến trình "dựa trên các điều kiện bình đẳng cho tất cả mọi người."

segments.src: - **Institutional readiness.** When a vote does take place, she said, the country's institutions "will be prepared to guarantee an inclusive and transparent process."
segments.tr: - **Sự sẵn sàng về mặt thể chế.** Khi một cuộc bỏ phiếu diễn ra, bà nói, các thể chế của đất nước "sẽ được chuẩn bị để đảm bảo một tiến trình bao trùm và minh bạch."

segments.src: - **A definition of democracy.** "Democracy is not measured by the mere existence of elections," she argued. It is measured, in her words, by the quality of the competition that comes before them.
segments.tr: - **Một định nghĩa về dân chủ.** "Dân chủ không được đo lường bằng việc đơn thuần có các cuộc bầu cử," bà lập luận. Theo lời bà, nó được đo lường bằng chất lượng của sự cạnh tranh diễn ra trước đó.

segments.src: - **A message of renewal.** "Today, Venezuela is being reborn," she said, while cautioning, "I do not promise you an easy way forward." She described rebuilding the country's "national soul" as a priority.
segments.tr: - **Một thông điệp về sự đổi mới.** "Hôm nay, Venezuela đang được tái sinh," bà nói, đồng thời cảnh báo, "Tôi không hứa với các bạn một con đường dễ dàng phía trước." Bà mô tả việc xây dựng lại "linh hồn quốc gia" của đất nước là một ưu tiên.

segments.src: - **Thanks to Washington.** She thanked President Donald Trump and his administration for their willingness to restore diplomatic ties and described a recent meeting as "historic." She named energy, economic cooperation, security and the fight against transnational crime as areas of shared interest, and called a recent oil agreement one of the largest ever reached between the two countries.
segments.tr: - **Lời cảm ơn gửi tới Washington.** Bà cảm ơn Tổng thống Donald Trump và chính quyền của ông vì sự sẵn lòng khôi phục quan hệ ngoại giao và mô tả cuộc gặp gần đây là "mang tính lịch sử." Bà nêu tên năng lượng, hợp tác kinh tế, an ninh và cuộc chiến chống tội phạm xuyên quốc gia là các lĩnh vực cùng quan tâm, và gọi một thỏa thuận dầu mỏ gần đây là một trong những thỏa thuận lớn nhất từng đạt được giữa hai nước.

segments.src: ## What she left out
segments.tr: ## Những gì bà đã bỏ qua

segments.src: Several observers noted the gaps as much as the promises.
segments.tr: Nhiều nhà quan sát lưu ý đến những khoảng trống cũng nhiều như những lời hứa.

segments.src: - **No date.** The most important detail for any election, the calendar, was absent. She offered no timeline and no benchmarks for setting one.
segments.tr: - **Không có ngày tháng.** Chi tiết quan trọng nhất cho bất kỳ cuộc bầu cử nào, lịch trình, đã vắng bóng. Bà không đưa ra mốc thời gian và không có tiêu chí nào để thiết lập một mốc thời gian.

segments.src: - **No named negotiating partners.** She referred to "opposition sectors" without identifying which groups are at the table.
segments.tr: - **Không nêu tên các đối tác đàm phán.** Bà đề cập đến "các thành phần đối lập" mà không xác định nhóm nào đang ngồi vào bàn đàm phán.

segments.src: - **No detail on judicial or electoral reform.** Independent analysts point out that credible elections usually depend on an updated voter roll and a restructured electoral authority. CSIS reports that no restructuring of the National Electoral Council has been discussed, and that voter rolls remain outdated.
segments.tr: - **Không có chi tiết về cải cách tư pháp hoặc bầu cử.** Các nhà phân tích độc lập chỉ ra rằng các cuộc bầu cử đáng tin cậy thường phụ thuộc vào danh sách cử tri được cập nhật và một cơ quan bầu cử được tái cơ cấu. CSIS báo cáo rằng không có cuộc tái cơ cấu nào đối với Hội đồng Bầu cử Quốc gia được thảo luận, và danh sách cử tri vẫn chưa được cập nhật.

segments.src: - **No direct response to the UN's own findings.** A UN fact-finding mission recently reported that Venezuela's repressive apparatus "remains entirely intact," and that rights violations continue despite improvements. Rodríguez's speech did not directly address that assessment.
segments.tr: - **Không phản hồi trực tiếp các phát hiện của chính LHQ.** Một phái đoàn tìm kiếm sự thật của LHQ gần đây đã báo cáo rằng bộ máy đàn áp của Venezuela "vẫn hoàn toàn nguyên vẹn" và các vi phạm quyền lợi vẫn tiếp diễn bất chấp những cải thiện. Bài phát biểu của Rodríguez không trực tiếp đề cập đến đánh giá đó.

segments.src: - **No mention of Maduro by name,** according to NBC News, a notable omission given that his capture is what brought her to office.
segments.tr: - **Không nhắc đến tên Maduro,** theo NBC News, một sự bỏ sót đáng chú ý khi việc ông bị bắt giữ chính là lý do đưa bà lên nắm quyền.

segments.src: ## The domestic picture
segments.tr: ## Bức tranh trong nước

segments.src: The speech landed in a country still under strain.
segments.tr: Bài phát biểu diễn ra trong bối cảnh đất nước vẫn đang chịu nhiều áp lực.

segments.src: CSIS describes the U.S.
segments.tr: CSIS mô tả cách tiếp cận của Mỹ

segments.src: approach after January as a three-stage plan of stabilization, recovery and transition.
segments.tr: sau tháng 1 là một kế hoạch ba giai đoạn gồm ổn định, phục hồi và chuyển giao.

segments.src: In its assessment, the first stage is largely complete, the second is underway but uneven, and the third, political transition, has stalled.
segments.tr: Trong đánh giá của mình, giai đoạn đầu tiên phần lớn đã hoàn thành, giai đoạn thứ hai đang được tiến hành nhưng không đồng đều, và giai đoạn thứ ba, chuyển giao chính trị, đã bị đình trệ.

segments.src: Some key data points from that analysis:
segments.tr: Một số điểm dữ liệu chính từ phân tích đó:

segments.src: - An amnesty law freed roughly one thousand detainees, but hundreds reportedly remain in custody.
segments.tr: - Một luật ân xá đã trả tự do cho khoảng một nghìn người bị giam giữ, nhưng hàng trăm người khác được báo cáo là vẫn đang bị giam giữ.

segments.src: - The U.S. eased oil-sector restrictions, opening the door to major energy investment.
segments.tr: - Mỹ đã nới lỏng các hạn chế đối với ngành dầu mỏ, mở đường cho các khoản đầu tư năng lượng lớn.

segments.src: - Ordinary Venezuelans have seen little relief. CSIS reports year-over-year inflation of about 534 percent and a frozen minimum wage that covers a tiny fraction of monthly food costs.
segments.tr: - Người dân Venezuela bình thường nhận được rất ít sự cứu trợ. CSIS báo cáo lạm phát so với cùng kỳ năm ngoái vào khoảng 534% và mức lương tối thiểu bị đóng băng chỉ đáp ứng được một phần nhỏ chi phí thực phẩm hàng tháng.

segments.src: The opposition is also divided.
segments.tr: Phe đối lập cũng bị chia rẽ.

segments.src: According to CSIS, one faction, led by Dinorah Figuera, is negotiating gradual institutional reforms.
segments.tr: Theo CSIS, một phe do Dinorah Figuera lãnh đạo đang đàm phán về các cải cách thể chế dần dần.

segments.src: Another, led by María Corina Machado, who has not been able to return to Venezuela, argues that the 2024 vote already settled the question of legitimacy and is pressing for immediate presidential elections.
segments.tr: Một phe khác do María Corina Machado lãnh đạo, người chưa thể trở lại Venezuela, lập luận rằng cuộc bỏ phiếu năm 2024 đã giải quyết xong câu hỏi về tính hợp pháp và đang thúc ép tổ chức bầu cử tổng thống ngay lập tức.

segments.src: Reports say a first round of talks between the opposition and the interim government began on August 6, and a second round started on September 15.
segments.tr: Các báo cáo cho biết vòng đàm phán đầu tiên giữa phe đối lập và chính phủ lâm thời đã bắt đầu vào ngày 6 tháng 8, và vòng thứ hai bắt đầu vào ngày 15 tháng 9.

segments.src: ## How Washington may respond
segments.tr: ## Washington có thể phản ứng thế nào

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: Lập trường của Mỹ

segments.src: position is not a single message.
segments.tr: không phải là một thông điệp duy nhất.

segments.src: Reporting points to at least two currents:
segments.tr: Các báo cáo chỉ ra ít nhất hai luồng ý kiến:

segments.src: 1. **The economic track.** President Trump has emphasized energy deals and normalized relations. He has also said Venezuela is "not ready yet" for elections, without offering a date. His conversation with Rodríguez was reported as warm and friendly, but also direct about the need for elections eventually.
segments.tr: 1. **Kênh kinh tế.** Tổng thống Trump đã nhấn mạnh các thỏa thuận năng lượng và bình thường hóa quan hệ. Ông cũng nói rằng Venezuela "vẫn chưa sẵn sàng" cho các cuộc bầu cử, mà không đưa ra ngày cụ thể. Cuộc trò chuyện của ông với Rodríguez được báo cáo là ấm áp và thân thiện, nhưng cũng trực tiếp về nhu cầu cuối cùng phải có bầu cử.

segments.src: 2. **The democratic-reform track.** Secretary of State Marco Rubio has stressed that "democratic elections are not simply about holding an election." He has cited conditions such as press freedom, freedom for all parties to organize, and reform of the electoral council. He has also suggested Venezuela's transition could move far faster than the multi-year transitions seen in Eastern Europe.
segments.tr: 2. **Kênh cải cách dân chủ.** Ngoại trưởng Marco Rubio nhấn mạnh rằng "các cuộc bầu cử dân chủ không đơn thuần là việc tổ chức một cuộc bầu cử." Ông đã dẫn ra các điều kiện như tự do báo chí, tự do tổ chức cho tất cả các đảng phái, và cải cách hội đồng bầu cử. Ông cũng gợi ý rằng quá trình chuyển giao của Venezuela có thể diễn ra nhanh hơn nhiều so với các quá trình chuyển giao kéo dài nhiều năm ở Đông Âu.

segments.src: CSIS argues these mixed signals may reduce the urgency of the political transition, and it raises a sequencing question: should institutional reforms come before long-term economic agreements, or after?
segments.tr: CSIS lập luận rằng những tín hiệu trái chiều này có thể làm giảm tính cấp bách của quá trình chuyển giao chính trị, và nó đặt ra câu hỏi về trình tự: liệu các cải cách thể chế nên diễn ra trước các thỏa thuận kinh tế dài hạn, hay sau đó?

segments.src: Supporters of the current approach say stability and investment come first.
segments.tr: Những người ủng hộ cách tiếp cận hiện tại nói rằng sự ổn định và đầu tư là ưu tiên hàng đầu.

segments.src: Critics worry that deals could outlast any democratic commitments.
segments.tr: Các nhà phê bình lo ngại rằng các thỏa thuận có thể tồn tại lâu hơn bất kỳ cam kết dân chủ nào.

segments.src: ## What to watch next
segments.tr: ## Những điều cần theo dõi tiếp theo

segments.src: - **An electoral calendar.** The clearest sign of progress would be a specific date or a published roadmap.
segments.tr: - **Một lịch trình bầu cử.** Dấu hiệu rõ ràng nhất của tiến trình sẽ là một ngày cụ thể hoặc một lộ trình được công bố.

segments.src: - **Electoral council reform and voter-roll updates.** These are practical prerequisites that outside observers will look for.
segments.tr: - **Cải cách hội đồng bầu cử và cập nhật danh sách cử tri.** Đây là những điều kiện tiên quyết thực tế mà các quan sát viên bên ngoài sẽ tìm kiếm.

segments.src: - **Outcomes from the opposition talks.** Whether the two rounds of negotiations produce written commitments, and whether the divided opposition can present a common position.
segments.tr: - **Kết quả từ các cuộc đàm phán của phe đối lập.** Liệu hai vòng đàm phán có đưa ra các cam kết bằng văn bản hay không, và liệu phe đối lập đang bị chia rẽ có thể đưa ra một lập trường chung hay không.

segments.src: - **Prisoner releases and press freedom.** Rubio's stated conditions give Washington measurable tests to apply.
segments.tr: - **Trả tự do cho tù nhân và tự do báo chí.** Các điều kiện nêu ra của Rubio cung cấp cho Washington các bài kiểm tra có thể đo lường được để áp dụng.

segments.src: - **U.S. policy coordination.** Whether the White House and the State Department align on how much weight to give elections relative to energy and security cooperation.
segments.tr: - **Sự phối hợp chính sách của Mỹ.** Liệu Nhà Trắng và Bộ Ngoại giao có thống nhất về mức độ coi trọng các cuộc bầu cử so với hợp tác năng lượng và an ninh hay không.

segments.src: ## Bottom line
segments.tr: ## Điểm mấu chốt

segments.src: Rodríguez's address gave the international community a public commitment it can now refer back to: elections will be held.
segments.tr: Bài phát biểu của Rodríguez đã đưa ra cho cộng đồng quốc tế một cam kết công khai mà giờ đây họ có thể đối chiếu: bầu cử sẽ được tổ chức.

segments.src: But a pledge without a date, a named process or concrete reforms leaves the central question open.
segments.tr: Nhưng một lời hứa không có ngày tháng, không có tiến trình cụ thể hay cải cách thực chất vẫn để ngỏ câu hỏi trung tâm.

segments.src: Whether September 23 is remembered as the start of a real transition or as a carefully worded holding statement will depend on what happens in the talks, in Caracas and in Washington over the coming months.
segments.tr: Liệu ngày 23 tháng 9 sẽ được nhớ đến như sự khởi đầu của một quá trình chuyển giao thực sự hay chỉ là một tuyên bố mang tính trì hoãn được diễn đạt cẩn thận sẽ phụ thuộc vào những gì diễn ra trong các cuộc đàm phán, tại Caracas và tại Washington trong những tháng tới.
